sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling with a randomized finite-support instrument conditional on each finite covariate stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are empirical within \((x,z)\); finite-sample inversion uses cellwise Clopper--Pearson intervals and asymptotics use their multinomial influence vectors.

body.tldr: Randomized minimax regret under partial identification is not new: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye already analyze randomized statistical rules in a finite-sample Gaussian-likelihood decision problem.  For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, this paper instead identifies the full categorical-instrument joint action-mean polytope and its complete population minimax correspondence.  The exact three-action witness has joint rule \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\) and value \(3/16\), whereas rectangularization selects \((0,0,1)\) with value \(1/4\); an exact rational matrix certifies all ten projected vertices, and uniform-response-type perturbations retain a value gap of at least \(1/32\) with full observed support.  On separated nondegenerate unique faces, the moving-response-basis and moving-coefficient plug-in map has a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian law.  At a displayed codimension-one face intersection, class-uniform honest contraction fails at every vanishing rate absent separation, while the Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union retains exact correspondence containment.

project_justification.gap: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye already supply a direct finite-sample Gaussian decision theory for randomized minimax-regret rules under partial identification, including multiplicity and least-randomizing refinements.  Song et al.'s model M1 supplies response-law compatibility restrictions for discrete instruments and outcomes.  Neither antecedent gives the sharp population minimax correspondence obtained by projecting a categorical-instrument response fiber, the derivative of the resulting plug-in optimizer when both feasible bases and regret coefficients move with the observable multinomial table, or exact confidence-fiber containment of that correspondence.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies the binary-outcome, finite-covariate-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1 and links its sharp joint response-type polytope to a finite randomized saddle program.  Its contribution is the categorical-IV population correspondence, moving-basis fixed-law inference on separated nondegenerate unique faces, and exact set-valued containment across face intersections.  It is not a claim of originating randomized minimax regret under partial identification and does not subsume Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye's finite-sample Gaussian admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing theory.
project_justification.fill: The exact response-fiber construction and feasible-basis program enumerate every population-optimal randomized mixture and expose observable pure-rule certificates.  The positive inference result gives an explicit moving-coefficient derivative and a uniform Gaussian policy-and-value law on separated nondegenerate unique faces; the negative result gives one internal codimension-one submodel on which uniform honest contraction at any vanishing rate is impossible without separation.  The exact Bonferroni confidence-fiber union supplies the noncontracting validity fallback.  An exact rational matrix certifies all ten vertices of the three-action witness, and a full-support perturbation supplies positive cell, treatment-support, variance, value-gap, and optimizer-separation margins.

body.related_work: Manski2000TreatmentChoice separates treatment choice from point identification, and Stoye2007ManyTreatments supplies the spike-state population allocation benchmark recovered here when every spike is feasible.  The closest direct decision-theoretic antecedent is MontielOleaQiuStoye2026DecisionTheory: it studies randomized minimax-regret statistical rules under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian likelihood, proves multiplicity results, and develops admissibility, least-randomizing, and profiled-regret refinements.  This paper neither claims the first randomized minimax-regret analysis under partial identification nor subsumes those results; it instead derives a sharp categorical-instrument population correspondence, a moving-response-basis and moving-coefficient fixed-law plug-in law, and exact correspondence containment.  Masten2023ManyTreatmentRules and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Asymptotics concern different repeated-sample or local-Gaussian treatment-choice problems.  Cui2021PartialIDDecisions randomizes a binary action from marginal contrast bounds; it does not optimize three or more actions against a joint categorical-instrument response polytope.  SongEtAl2026CategoricalIV supplies model M1's response-law compatibility restrictions; the present model is its binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization.  SachsEtAl2023SymbolicBounds and MastinJailletChin2014RandomizedRegret provide the response-function linear-program and finite-saddle ingredients, whose composition is background.  HruzaEtAl2026CategoricalPIL studies a broader overlapping bound-agnostic class and releases a multicategory implementation; the exact and full-support perturbed witnesses are concrete regression targets for its coordinatewise-rectangle decision rule, while the present response-basis and KKT theorem does not transfer by class inclusion.  BonnansShapiro2000Perturbation informs the separated-face analysis; KlattMunkZemel2022RandomLP and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023LPConfidence concern adjacent fixed-coefficient formulations; FangSantos2019DirectionalInference motivates derivative-aware inference for nonsmooth maps.  No named method is claimed to be refuted by the internal face-intersection result.  ClopperPearson1934Binomial and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007Sets inform the exact, noncontracting confidence-fiber fallback.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian policy-and-regret law is restricted to the observable nondegenerate unique-face class with fixed-support, response-basis, rank, slack, reduced-cost, and active-weight margins.  It is a fixed-law plug-in result for a categorical-instrument moving polytope, not a replacement for Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye's finite-sample Gaussian admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing analysis.  The face-intersection theorem is existential and internal to the maintained model: one displayed codimension-one local submodel rules out the specified class-uniform honest contraction at every vanishing rate absent separation.  The Bonferroni confidence-fiber union remains valid but may be conservative and noncontracting.  For the perturbed witness, only a gap of at least \(1/32\) and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods are guaranteed; the exact \(1/16\) gap and exact optimizer formulas are asserted only at \(\delta=0\).
body.honest_scope: The maintained causal model is the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, with finite randomized instrument support, categorical treatment, response-type exogeneity, consistency, exclusion, positive stratum--instrument support, and response-fiber compatibility.  Response-function projection and finite randomized-regret programming are background ingredients.  Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye already analyze randomized minimax-regret statistical decisions under partial identification in a finite-sample Gaussian likelihood; this paper claims neither priority for that decision criterion nor coverage of their admissibility, profiled-regret, or least-randomizing theory.  The delivered objects are the sharp categorical-IV population optimizer correspondence, its moving-basis fixed-law limit law on separated nondegenerate unique faces, and exact confidence-fiber correspondence containment.  Without separation, only an internal existential face-intersection obstruction is claimed.  The exact three-action counterexample is supplemented by full-support perturbations, but its exact optimizer identities and exact \(1/16\) gap are not claimed to persist after perturbation.
body.interpretation: The exact witness shows why joint partial-identification geometry matters for categorical treatment choice: the feasible inequality \(\mu_0\leq\mu_2\) changes both the optimal randomized policy and its sharp worst-case regret relative to coordinatewise rectangularization.  A single exact rational matrix simultaneously verifies compatibility and projection for all ten vertices, including the two laws questioned in review.  The uniform-response-type perturbation shows that the failure persists with positive observed cells, positive treatment support, and nondegenerate conditional outcomes, although only a conservative \(1/32\) value gap and disjoint optimizer neighborhoods are asserted away from the exact law.  The decision-theoretic act of randomized minimax regret under partial identification has a direct antecedent in Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye; what is specific here is the categorical-IV joint-polytope correspondence and its moving-polytope fixed-law inference.  Separated unique faces admit ordinary root-\(n\) Gaussian analysis, whereas exact confidence-fiber containment remains the appropriate validity claim at face intersections.
